newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's says 1.4 bln stg sold in capacity auctions.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's says 1.4 bln stg sold in capacity auctions.

text.p: Lloyd's of London on Friday provided evidence of increased investor demand for space on its insurance syndicates since the completion of its recovery plan.

The insurance market said that over 1.4 billion stg worth of capacity was traded during this year's eight capacity auctions, which took place from July to October. Capacity is the amount of business the market can underwrite in terms of premium income.
While last year's auction period lasted only a few weeks and total capacity traded was a much smaller 250 million stg, the prices paid this year were significantly higher.

The average weighted value of one pound of capacity in the 1996 auctions was 2.4 pence compared to 1.4 pence last year, and prices ranged to over 20 pence for some syndicates during the final two auctions, when supply was scarce.

Lloyd's in September successfully completed its recovery plan after more than 90 percent of its backers, known as Names, decided to accept a 3.2 billion stg out of court settlement offer designed to compensate them for previous crippling losses.

Market sources said the increased interest in the auctions and the higher prices paid for space on syndicates was as much a reflection of recent confidence in Lloyd's future as recognition that the auction process was really the only way in this year.

The auctions were introduced in 1995 and are designed to give members the opportunity to realise value from their participation on syndicates. They were previously unable to do so when they resigned from the market. "The whole of the market has been much more geared up," said one syndicate analyst. "By the time it started, it was clear that R&R (Reconstruction and Renewal) was going to go through."
Several analysts suggested the higher prices paid for capacity meant that fewer Names were leaving the market this year than had been expected to do so.
"They've actually seen that Lloyd's can make money. The predictions for 1994 and 1995 are good," said another analyst.

He ventured the drop might be in the region of about 2,000 Names. There are 12,000 Names active currently. Lloyd's is not expected to know how many have left until the end of the year. Lloyd's in July reported record earnings of nearly 1.1 billion stg, ending five years of disastrous losses totalling more than 8.0 billion stg.
The insurance market said then it expected a profit of 1.0 billion stg for the 1994 year and nearly 0.9 billion for 1995.
The market reports three years in arrears to allow time for claims processing.
The eighth and final capacity auction, which began on Monday and finished on Thursday, saw 73 million stg of capacity auctioned successfully, realising a value of 3.9 million.
Buy orders totalled 206 million stg and sell orders 98 million.
